name: Tahpenes
overview: Tahpenes is a female figure identified as the Queen of Egypt, mentioned specifically in 1 Kings 11:19. While Scripture provides limited information about her background or tribe, her position as queen marks her as a notable personage within the biblical narrative. No additional personal notes or tribal affiliations are recorded for her.
namesAndTitles: The name Tahpenes is a proper name that means "wife of the king," reflecting her royal status. This name is not indicated as being given by God but highlights her role within the Egyptian monarchy as documented in 1 Kings 11:19.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Tahpenes as the wife of Pharaoh, establishing her as the queen consort of Egypt. Beyond this marital relationship, no further family connections or descendants are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tahpenes holds significance as a representative of Egypt's royal household during the time of King Solomon, illustrating the political and cultural interactions between Israel and Egypt. Her mention underscores the broader narrative of international alliances and relationships in the biblical account. Though details are sparse, her role as queen provides context for understanding the geopolitical environment of the era.
